inspection_summary: Inspected all 2,727 logical lines. The article starts from a polynomial transform whose symmetric outputs may have all zeros on Re(s)=1/2, passes through higher-order recurrences and real-root/interlacing questions, and unexpectedly reaches moments, Hankel determinants, Macdonald-type integrals, alternating sign matrices, and lattice paths. Its strongest polynomial-zero result proves the C≥3 half of a conjecture for one renormalized four-term recurrence; necessity, the original quadratic polynomial-RH claim, the five-term C=6 analogue, and broader interlacing statements remain conjectural or numerical. The recurrence-to-combinatorics chain contains numerous proved bijections and determinant identities, but the Robbins–Rumsey evaluation uses computer-generated summation certificates, one preserved only by an external link. Twenty-nine units separate proved combinatorics, polynomial-RH analogies, conjectures, computations, and heuristic renormalization. These polynomial ‘Riemann hypotheses’ are analogies, not results about ζ. Formula extraction frequently corrupts halves, fractional powers, binomial coefficients, determinants, signs, contour branches, and long certificates; exact reuse requires the PDF and, for the automated proof, its external certificate artifact.

sections_inspected.label: Title, abstract, and publication front matter
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Summarizes polynomial recurrences, moments, determinants, ASM connections, and path models; otherwise metadata.

sections_inspected.label: Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the polynomial transform and polynomial-RH analogy, states the quadratic conjectural program, explains renormalization, and maps the proved/conjectural combinatorial equality chain.

sections_inspected.label: The 3-Conjecture
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives the normalized four-term recurrence, contrasts three-term orthogonality, states the iff conjecture, and proves real-root interlacing for C≥3.

sections_inspected.label: The 6-Conjecture
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States a five-term C≥6 real-root/interlacing conjecture supported only by numerical evidence.

sections_inspected.label: Moments
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the recurrence functional and proves nine algebraic, path, tree, coefficient, contour, real-integral, and binomial characterizations of its moments.

sections_inspected.label: Very special Hankel determinants
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Computes critical C=3 determinants, records finite agreement with vertically symmetric ASM numbers, and proposes positivity/statistic refinements in t.

sections_inspected.label: Positivity is insufficient
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Constructs a positive functional supporting a four-term recurrence with a polynomial having non-real zeros.

sections_inspected.label: Macdonald-type integrals
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Converts the critical Hankel determinant to a Vandermonde-square multiple integral and an equivalent determinant of explicit binomial moments.

sections_inspected.label: Equivalent determinant forms
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Proves several Hankel representations, evaluates the determinant as the Robbins–Rumsey product using an LDU/WZ computation, and notes conjectural t-deformations.

sections_inspected.label: ASM, vertical symmetry, and path models
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Reviews ASM enumeration, develops non-intersecting/osculating path machinery, and bijects vertically symmetric ASMs with a specified osculating-path family.

sections_inspected.label: Path interpretations and Hankel determinants
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses modified sign-reversing involutions to count Hankel determinants by non-intersecting paths, proves a Catalan-Hankel evaluation, and records tableau encodings and a missing direct bijection.

sections_inspected.label: Higher-order determinants
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Computes the C=6 moment determinants and reports numerical smoothness/non-smoothness observations for broader binomial Hankel families.

sections_inspected.label: Epilogue and twisted transform
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Summarizes the research program and states a cited polynomial-RH preservation result for a multidimensional twisted transform while leaving interlacing open.

sections_inspected.label: Appendix I: recurrence derivation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives the original four-term recurrence from differential identities for the integral transform.

sections_inspected.label: Appendix II: asymptotic renormalization
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Performs a sequence of asymptotic scalings and replacements leading from the original recurrence to the one-parameter normalized recurrence and critical C=3.

accepted_units.title: A symmetry-preserving polynomial transform creates a critical-line zero problem
accepted_units.why_material: The linear transform maps monomials to rising-factorial polynomials and has an integral representation; symmetric input gives the functional equation T[g](s)=T[g](1−s). The source defines a polynomial ‘Riemann hypothesis’ as all zeros lying on Re(s)=1/2 and cites a prior preservation theorem when the input already has that property.
accepted_units.context_note: The cited preservation result and earlier three-term proof are background, not proved here; no claim concerns zeros of the Riemann zeta function.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Integral normalization, rising factorial, the half shift, and coefficient-positivity expansion contain damaged fractions and require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: The quadratic transform leads to a four-term recurrence and an unproved interlacing RH analogue
accepted_units.why_material: For powers of x(x−1)+r, the transformed polynomial becomes a real polynomial in u=−t² on the critical line. Numerical evidence suggests negative real zeros and interlacing, but the four-term recurrence lacks standard orthogonality. An asymptotic renormalization compresses n,r dependence to one parameter C and motivates a threshold conjecture.
accepted_units.context_note: The quadratic polynomial RH, coefficient positivity, and higher-order extensions are explicitly unproved; only one half of the renormalized threshold conjecture is proved later.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The r≥1/4 range, u substitution, coefficient expansion, and C relation are formula-sensitive; verify them from the PDF.

accepted_units.title: One critical Hankel sequence links recurrences, integrals, determinants, ASMs, and two path models
accepted_units.why_material: The introduction isolates the sequence 1,3,26,646,45885 and states the later proved identities Δ=I=A=RR, V=O, and A=P. It also identifies a still-missing direct bijection between the osculating and non-intersecting path families as an alternative combinatorial proof of the vertically symmetric ASM formula.
accepted_units.context_note: The chain mixes theorems proved in this article with the externally proved identity V=RR; the direct O↔P bijection is proposed, not supplied.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The Robbins–Rumsey product and indexing shifts are damaged in extraction; check exact sequence conventions and equality indices in the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Renormalization replaces the original n-dependent recurrence by q_n=xq_{n−1}−Cq_{n−2}−q_{n−3}
accepted_units.why_material: The section records the exact original four-term recurrence and the normalized one-parameter recurrence obtained by the appendix transformations, with the original r range mapped toward a critical limiting value C=3.
accepted_units.context_note: The normalized recurrence is rigorously studied as its own sequence, but its derivation from the original quadratic family is asymptotic and includes discarded terms; it does not transfer Theorem 1 back to the original polynomial-RH conjecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Coefficients, fractional powers in C(r), and sign conventions differ visibly between displays and appendices; verify the exact normalizations from the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Three-term positivity forces interlacing, but four-term functionals lose the needed orthogonality
accepted_units.why_material: The standard three-term recurrence yields a positive-definite orthogonality functional exactly when its recurrence coefficients are positive, hence simple real interlacing zeros and positive Hankel determinants. The analogous functional for the four-term recurrence annihilates each q_n but not cross-products, identifying why the classical proof cannot transfer.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a conceptual comparison, not a general theorem that every higher recurrence fails; the explicit failure of positivity sufficiency appears later.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Functional normalization, λ products, and determinant indexing require PDF checking due to missing inequality and not-equal glyphs.

accepted_units.title: The 3-Conjecture asserts an iff threshold, while Theorem 1 proves only C≥3
accepted_units.why_material: Conjecture 1 claims real zeros exactly for C≥3 and interlacing in that regime. The source proves sufficiency but reports only numerical non-real zeros below 3, including near C=2.9, leaving necessity open.
accepted_units.context_note: This span is retained to prevent the theorem from being misreported as the full iff conjecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The statement is prose-stable; exact indexing and strict/non-strict threshold should still be verified.

accepted_units.title: A continuity transition and characteristic-root case split prove interlacing for C≥3
accepted_units.why_material: For fixed finite N, large C gives a perturbation of orthogonal polynomials. Any first loss of strict interlacing must create a common real root of consecutive q’s. Solving the recurrence at that root through a cubic characteristic equation forces a repeated characteristic root; distinct, double, and triple-root cases show such a transition cannot occur at or above 3.
accepted_units.context_note: The finite-N argument is arbitrary and therefore yields all q_n. The proof is for the normalized recurrence only.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula risk: scaling powers, determinant conditions, characteristic-root parametrization, geometric sums, and double-root inequalities are fragmented. Exact proof reconstruction requires the PDF.

accepted_units.title: The 6-Conjecture proposes a C≥6 threshold for a five-term recurrence
accepted_units.why_material: A representative higher-order recurrence is conjectured to have real interlacing zeros exactly above the binomial-looking threshold 6, suggesting a wider family of critical coefficients.
accepted_units.context_note: No half of this conjecture is proved in the source; support is described only as substantial numerical evidence, and the binomial-coefficient pattern is speculative.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The recurrence signs and initial indices are readable but should be PDF-checked.

accepted_units.title: One recurrence functional has nine algebraic, combinatorial, and analytic moment forms
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 2 identifies the moments of the four-term functional as an inverse coefficient-matrix entry, weighted excursions, 2–3 trees, a Lagrange coefficient, an explicit sum, a positive real integral for C≥3, and three special C=3 integral/binomial expressions. This is the principal bridge from recurrence theory to combinatorics.
accepted_units.context_note: All nine items are theorem claims; the density’s explicit positivity at C≥3 is essential for later functional positivity but does not alone force real zeros for arbitrary four-term recurrences.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high formula risk: steps/weights, coefficient extraction, multinomial indices, branch roots, fractional powers, and binomial sums are corrupted. Verify every item from the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Inverse coefficients become weighted paths, 2–3 trees, and a Lagrange functional equation
accepted_units.why_material: The proof inverts the recurrence coefficient matrix, reads its recursion as a weighted nonnegative path model, bijects paths with depth-first codes of 2–3 trees, and decomposes trees into two or three principal subtrees. Lagrange inversion then supplies the coefficient and multinomial moment formulas; a contour-generating-function derivation gives an independent check.
accepted_units.context_note: This proves items 1–5 of Theorem 2 and provides the combinatorial reason for nonnegative integer coefficients in C.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Matrix recurrences, path step directions, contour orientation, generating-function denominator, and coefficient indices are extraction-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Contour deformation yields a positive real moment density exactly in the C≥3 regime
accepted_units.why_material: The contour representation is analyzed through the cubic inverse map and its discriminant. For C>3, branch points and cycles permit deformation to a real interval where the branch jump defines a positive density; the degenerate C=3 case follows by a limit and explicit substitutions.
accepted_units.context_note: This proves items 6–7 and positivity of the specific recurrence functional. It does not prove the below-3 necessity in the zero conjecture or positivity⇒interlacing for general four-term recurrences.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extreme branch/formula risk: cubic radicals, discriminant, root ordering, contour geometry, fractional powers, and substitutions are severely fragmented; PDF/figure verification is mandatory.

accepted_units.title: Further substitutions convert critical moments to fractional-binomial sums and degree data
accepted_units.why_material: The proof transforms the C=3 integral to a beta-type integral, producing the remaining fractional-binomial expression; the final form is stated with details omitted. Path and multinomial views then determine degrees and leading Catalan/binomial coefficients of the moment polynomials.
accepted_units.context_note: Item 8 is derived; the source explicitly omits details for item 9, so that expression is a stated theorem result without a complete local derivation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Substitutions, beta integral, signs, fractional binomial coefficients, and leading-term formulas are highly extraction-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Critical Hankel data match vertically symmetric ASM counts and suggest a positive t-statistic
accepted_units.why_material: At C=3 the moment Hankel determinants compute the striking ASM-number prefix. Explicit low-n polynomials Δ_n(3+t) have nonnegative coefficients even though Δ_n(C) does not; the authors conjecturally interpret t as a statistic on a larger object class.
accepted_units.context_note: Finite determinant formulas and coefficients are computed; general coefficient nonnegativity, the t-statistic, and the initial ASM identification at this point are conjectural/data-driven. A product evaluation is proved later.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Determinant polynomials, degrees, and large coefficients are vulnerable to OCR/transcription errors; verify all data from the PDF or recompute.

accepted_units.title: A positive functional can support a four-term recurrence with non-real zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Starting from Hermite orthogonality, the authors perturb finitely many basis polynomials so the same positive functional annihilates the new recurrence sequence, then choose explicit parameters making q_4 vanish at a non-real point. This disproves the naive extension of the three-term positivity criterion.
accepted_units.context_note: The counterexample is explicit and proved; it does not contradict positivity’s sufficiency for the special C≥3 recurrence, where interlacing has an independent proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Parameter conditions, γ formula, and the explicit complex zero should be verified against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Andreief/Vandermonde symmetrization turns Δ_n into a Macdonald-type integral
accepted_units.why_material: Substituting the one-variable moment integral into the Hankel determinant and symmetrizing over variables converts the product of two determinants to a squared Vandermonde, yielding Theorem 3’s multiple integral I_n.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem proves Δ_n=I_n. The subsequent statement that these integrals count vertically symmetric ASMs is conditional on the other equality chain, not a direct integral bijection.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Normalization powers, integration domain, Vandermonde variables, and density exponents are formula-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Termwise beta evaluation gives a binomial-moment determinant
accepted_units.why_material: Expanding the squared Vandermonde and evaluating each density moment by beta/gamma identities identifies Δ_n with a Hankel determinant whose entries are explicit integer binomial expressions, illustrated through n=2.
accepted_units.context_note: This calculation supplies the first form used by Theorem 4; examples support but are not substitutes for the general symmetrized identity.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Composition coefficients, gamma ratios, determinant indexing, and binomial M_k are densely damaged; PDF verification is required.

accepted_units.title: Row operations produce four equivalent Hankel moment sequences, one parameter-independent
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 4 transforms the original moments to explicit binomial sequences and a polynomial family b_k(x). A Carlitz recurrence plus degree counting shows det[b_{i+j}(x)] is independent of x, so specializations yield three further Hankel forms.
accepted_units.context_note: The determinant invariance and four representations are proved; the combinatorial interpretation of the t-deformed determinant discussed next is not.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Binomial forms, gamma calculation, Carlitz arrays, recurrence (29), and degree argument require exact PDF checking.

accepted_units.title: Equivalent t-deformed Hankel entries are proposed but not constructed
accepted_units.why_material: The observed nonnegative Δ_n(3+t) coefficients motivate the idea that each equivalent critical moment sequence should admit a polynomial t-deformation with the same determinant.
accepted_units.context_note: This is explicitly a reasonable assumption/speculation; no a_k(t), determinant identity, or statistic is supplied.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mostly prose; the referenced binomial entry and t normalization should be checked.

accepted_units.title: An LDU ansatz and WZ certificates evaluate Δ_n as the Robbins–Rumsey product
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 5 chooses an explicit lower-triangular multiplier that should triangularize the binomial Hankel matrix, reducing the determinant to diagonal factors matching RR(n). The required off-diagonal and diagonal multisums are certified by Wilf–Zeilberger-style recurrences generated with automated tools.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem is presented as proved, but the multiplier was guessed and checked numerically up to 30×30 before automation; one certificate is printed, while the much larger diagonal certificate is only linked externally and is not preserved in this normalized source. Independent verification is therefore unavailable here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extreme risk: the multiplier, factorial multisums, certificates, boundary conventions, and product diagonal are heavily corrupted. The external 1.2MB certificate and original PDF/code are required for audit.

accepted_units.title: Vertically symmetric ASMs realize the Robbins–Rumsey sequence by an external theorem
accepted_units.why_material: The section defines ASMs, recalls the general enumeration, and states the product for odd-size vertically symmetric ASMs. The product is the same RR(n) evaluated by Theorem 5.
accepted_units.context_note: The V=RR identity is prior work attributed to Kuperberg, not proved in this article. It completes a numerical equality chain but not a direct bijection to the article’s Hankel paths.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Product formulas, size shift 2n+3, and historical status need PDF/reference verification.

accepted_units.title: Sign-reversing involutions count non-intersecting paths, while corner sums encode ASMs as osculating paths
accepted_units.why_material: The source reviews the Lindström-style signed path determinant and its path-tail switching involution, then converts ASM row/column partial-sum constraints into level boundaries of the corner-sum matrix. Those boundaries form osculating rather than non-intersecting paths.
accepted_units.context_note: This supplies the common language for the two path families; the general determinant count needs endpoint-order hypotheses, which later fail and must be repaired.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Endpoint coordinates, binomial determinant orientation, corner-sum index convention, and path directions are formula/figure dependent.

accepted_units.title: Vertically symmetric ASMs are bijective with a fixed osculating-path ensemble
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 2 restricts the corner-sum construction to half of a vertically symmetric ASM, where the central column and boundary data force specified starts and ends. The remaining cell boundaries give an osculating family, and the map is reversible.
accepted_units.context_note: This proves V_n=O_n. It does not biject these osculating paths to the non-intersecting Hankel paths introduced next.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Matrix size/index shifts, start/end coordinates, forced rows/columns, and the figure are essential and should be PDF-checked.

accepted_units.title: A two-stage cancellation rescues a path determinant when the standard endpoint criterion fails
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 6 interprets a family of binomial Hankel determinants. Because non-identity path matchings can be non-intersecting, ordinary tail-switching is insufficient; a first involution uses a binomial divisibility bijection to cancel paths beginning with too many vertical steps, after which standard intersection cancellation leaves exactly ordered non-intersecting paths.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem is proved for every integer r≥1; vertically symmetric ASM-related determinants are the r=2 case. The ‘nice’ elementary bijection used for division is assumed selectable rather than explicitly constructed in detail.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Endpoint coordinates, binomial identities (40)–(42), signs, and fixed-point characterization are figure/formula dependent.

accepted_units.title: Hankel paths realize the ASM-number determinant and yield a Catalan determinant proof
accepted_units.why_material: The r=2 specialization defines P_n and proves it equals the critical binomial determinant. A related two-stage symmetric involution shows another central-binomial Hankel determinant counts 2^n right-angle path families, while the r=1 case gives a combinatorial proof that a Catalan Hankel determinant equals one.
accepted_units.context_note: These are proved determinant/path counts. Equality P_n=O_n follows only indirectly through product evaluations; a direct path bijection remains absent.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Determinant entries, exponent 2^n, symmetric-point involution, and indexing shifts are extraction-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Both path models admit tableau encodings, but their equality lacks a direct bijection
accepted_units.why_material: Non-intersecting Hankel paths correspond to bounded column-strict staircase tableaux, while osculating ASM paths correspond to strict Gelfand patterns or shifted ‘good’ tableaux. These parallel encodings sharpen the proposed bijection problem.
accepted_units.context_note: Each within-model correspondence is asserted as straightforward; the source does not construct a bijection between the two tableau families F1 and F2.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Shapes, row bounds, and index shifts are tied to figures and should be checked in the PDF.

accepted_units.title: C=6 determinants have alternate binomial forms, while broader smoothness patterns appear to fail
accepted_units.why_material: The five-term critical recurrence defines a moment functional whose first Hankel determinants match a higher-r binomial determinant row. Numerical factorization suggests the exceptional smooth product behavior at low orders does not persist for general binomial parameters a≥4.
accepted_units.context_note: Initial moments/determinants and an alternate form are stated as readily checkable; general equality, critical real-root behavior, and non-smoothness are computational observations/conjectures, not proved theorems here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Signs of moments, determinant values, binomial parameters, and ‘largest prime factor’ data should be recomputed or PDF-verified.

accepted_units.title: A multidimensional twisted transform preserves polynomial critical-line zeros, but interlacing remains open
accepted_units.why_material: The epilogue generalizes the one-variable transform to a coupled multidimensional kernel and cites a proof that critical-line-rooted input polynomials yield a critical-line-rooted output. The expected interlacing phenomenon and associated combinatorics are deferred.
accepted_units.context_note: The twisted-transform preservation theorem belongs to cited work [9], not a proof in this paper; the interlacing claim is explicitly unproved.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Kernel exponents, multidimensional measure, transform normalization, and implication quantifiers are heavily extracted and require the cited source/PDF.

accepted_units.title: Differentiating a transformed integral derives the original four-term recurrence
accepted_units.why_material: Appendix I embeds the transform in a one-parameter group of interval maps, differentiates its multiplier at the identity, and specializes to powers of a quadratic. Differential identities for those powers produce the exact n,r-dependent four-term recurrence and indicate a route to higher-order recurrences.
accepted_units.context_note: This appendix derives the original recurrence exactly; it does not establish its polynomial-RH conjecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Invariant measure, group map, derivatives, and recurrence coefficients are formula-sensitive and partly malformed; exact derivation needs the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Successive asymptotic scalings explain—but do not rigorously transfer—the critical C=3 model
accepted_units.why_material: Appendix II sets s=1/2+it and u=−t², then divides by n², discards vanishing coefficient terms, rescales variables and polynomials, and replaces n-dependent arguments to obtain a constant-coefficient four-term recurrence. The r>1/4 range maps to C>3, explaining why 3 emerged as the normalized threshold.
accepted_units.context_note: The source explicitly ‘throws away’ terms and replaces one recurrence by another; this is an asymptotic modeling heuristic, not a limit theorem proving that zeros/interlacing of the normalized q_n control the original P_n. A sign reflection relates two versions of the final model exactly.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Extreme formula risk: every rescaling, fractional power, sign, n-dependent argument, and r-to-C map must be checked from the PDF before formal asymptotic analysis.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The critical value C=3 sits at three different interfaces
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: For the normalized four-term recurrence, C=3 is simultaneously the proved onset of real interlacing, the degenerate endpoint of a positive integral density, and the parameter where the Hankel determinants acquire the vertically symmetric ASM sequence.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Only the normalized recurrence theorem and moment/determinant facts are proved; the passage back to the original quadratic polynomial RH is heuristic, and the general t-statistic interpretation is conjectural.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Positivity and real-rootedness decouple beyond three-term orthogonality
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Three-term recurrences use positive orthogonality to force interlacing, whereas the four-term functional loses cross-orthogonality; the special C≥3 sequence still interlaces by a transition argument, but an explicit Hermite-based construction shows positivity alone cannot explain it.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The counterexample rules out a general positivity criterion, not a more specialized higher-order structure for this recurrence.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A recurrence moment is a hub of representations
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The same moments arise from inverse recurrence coefficients, weighted excursions, 2–3 trees, Lagrange inversion, contour jumps, positive densities, beta integrals, and explicit binomial sequences; taking their Hankel determinant transports identities between these domains.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Some late fractional-binomial details are omitted locally, and exact analytic branch manipulations are formula-dependent.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The ASM equality chain is proved algebraically but lacks the desired direct bijection
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Critical Hankel determinants equal the Robbins–Rumsey product by a computer-assisted triangularization, prior work equates that product with vertically symmetric ASMs, and this paper separately models the two sides by non-intersecting and osculating paths. A direct bijection between those path/tableau families would replace the product-mediated equality.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: No direct bijection is given, and the diagonal WZ certificate needed to audit the determinant evaluation is external to the source.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Nonstandard endpoint geometry calls for layered involutions
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: When ordinary path-tail switching leaves non-identity non-intersecting matchings, a preliminary sign-reversing involution removes a structurally forbidden boundary or symmetry class; standard intersection cancellation then exposes a positive fixed-point family counted by the determinant.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The first involution in Theorem 6 depends on choosing a combinatorial division bijection that is not made explicit, limiting direct constructivity.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Polynomial RH terminology names a finite zero analogy, not zeta evidence
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Functional equations about s↔1−s motivate asking whether polynomial zeros lie on Re(s)=1/2; variable changes turn this into real-root/interlacing problems for recurrence polynomials, with threshold conjectures and one proved normalized case.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: None of these results bears directly on the truth of the Riemann hypothesis for ζ, and several advertised analogues remain numerical or conjectural.
